status: draft process-lifetime deletion guard tested in isolation; no Chromium deletion hooks are installed
implementation: root-bound shared guard defaults to defer until verified store identity is confirmed by native registry
exact Personal directory is protected, invalid paths denied, and validated non-Personal action runs under same lock as invalidation
a changed Personal path or UUID is refused; invalidation makes further actions defer until same identity reverified
POSIX compares directory device/inode to prevent case aliases of Personal being treated as named, rejecting symlinks, absent targets and non-directories
Windows and unqualified platforms defer named deletion pending native handle/reparse-point qualification
registry draft confirms gate from the verified identity even when Personal is not loaded; the separately owned gate can outlive registry shutdown
verified: isolated fake action never runs for unknown identity, Personal, unsafe path, symlink, nonexistent or non-directory target
named action can run with distinct observed POSIX directory identities; failed action preserves synthetic cleanup marker
reassignment and changed UUID refused; invalidation defers until exact identity restored
concurrent invalidation waits while a guarded action holds the lock, and following actions defer
private gate confirmation rejected by compiler; registry and factory pass syntax checks
upstreamDeletionPaths: DeleteProfileHelper::MaybeScheduleProfileForDeletion can close windows/cancel downloads before eventual cleanup
startup PreProfileInit calls CleanUpEphemeralProfiles and CleanUpDeletedProfiles before loaded Profile/registry
browser_shutdown::ShutdownPostThreadsStop calls NukeDeletedProfilesFromDisk after g_browser_process is gone
NukeProfileFromDisk is also used by new-profile creation for an unused target; a blanket hook can break creation
deferred cleanup must retain kProfilesDeleted/ephemeral bookkeeping and must not run success callbacks or remove attributes
limitations: guard is not connected to any real deletion entry point or startup/shutdown plumbing; it currently protects no user profile
POSIX lstat checks and callback are not bound to a directory handle; an external replacement between check and operation remains possible
callbacks hold a lock; production scheduling must avoid blocking UI/teardown and avoid reentrancy while serializing invalidation and destructive work
identity must load early enough to defer startup cleanup and guard must outlive BrowserProcess for post-thread cleanup
native deletion UI must veto Personal before marking, closing windows or cancelling downloads; named cleanup must resume safely after deferred identity resolution
Windows handle/reparse support, real ProfileManager lifecycle, fault injection and Linux/Windows runtime tests remain open
